content: Aprepitant is indicated for the prevention of both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC), including high-dose cisplatin, as well as moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (MEC). For oral suspension: Safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 6 months of age. Children must be able to swallow capsules whole. Chronic continuous administration is not recommended due to lack of study and potential changes in the drug interaction profile over prolonged use. Drug interactions: 1. Chloramphenicol: Increases aprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraindicated. 2. Darunavir: Increases aprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 3. Flibanserin: Aprepitant increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to risks of severe hypotension or syncope. 4. Lomitapide: Aprepitant increases lomitapide levels several-fold via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 5. Lonafarnib: Aprepitant increases lonafarnib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 6. Pimozide: Aprepitant increases pimozide levels by reducing its metabolism, leading to a risk of QT interval prolongation. Contraindicated. 7. Ribociclib: Increases aprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 8. Tipranavir: Increases aprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 9. Apalutamide: Decreases aprepitant levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce therapeutic efficacy. 10. Avapritinib: Aprepitant increases avapritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the avapritinib starting dose. 11. Axitinib: Aprepitant increases axitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely and adjust the dose as necessary. 12.
